mechanism_narrative: A rise in GDP indicates increased economic activity, leading to higher demand for goods and services, which in turn drives up stock prices, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative during periods of GDP growth, or the correlation between GDP and S&P 500 returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4%, it indicates a tightening monetary policy, leading to decreased borrowing and spending, which negatively impacts stock prices, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive when the federal funds rate is above 4%, or the federal funds rate does not significantly impact stock prices (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate indicates a weakening labor market, leading to decreased consumer spending and economic activity, which negatively impacts stock prices, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive during periods of rising unemployment, or the correlation between unemployment and S&P 500 returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production indicates increased economic activity, leading to higher demand for goods and services, which in turn drives up stock prices, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative during periods of increased industrial production, or the correlation between industrial production and S&P 500 returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts and GDP are both increasing, it indicates a strong demand for goods and services, leading to higher stock prices, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative when housing starts and GDP are both increasing, or the interaction between housing starts and GDP does not significantly impact stock prices (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is below 3% and the CPI is increasing, it indicates an expansionary monetary policy, leading to increased borrowing and spending, which positively impacts stock prices, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 3% and CPIAUCSL rises > 0.2pp in 2 months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative when the federal funds rate is below 3% and the CPI is increasing, or the interaction between the federal funds rate and CPI does not significantly impact stock prices (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate is below 4% and payroll employment is increasing, it indicates a strong labor market, leading to increased consumer spending and economic activity, which positively impacts stock prices, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative when the unemployment rate is below 4% and payroll employment is increasing, or the interaction between the unemployment rate and payroll employment does not significantly impact stock prices (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When retail sales and GDP are both increasing, it indicates a strong demand for goods and services, leading to higher stock prices, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, but only during periods of monetary easing.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative when retail sales and GDP are both increasing during periods of monetary easing, or the interaction between retail sales and GDP does not significantly impact stock prices (t-test p > 0.05).
